# deed_source (Resource)

A Deed source: a connector Deed pulls from on a schedule (`github`, `hallpass`, `porch`, `terraform_state`, `pulse_admin`, `pulse_tail`, …) or a push source that external programs feed through source tokens. Requires the project `admin` role (or an installation admin token). The provider's configuration schema, secret fields and defaults are listed by `GET /api/v1/providers` and on the source page in the UI.

Credentials go in `secrets_wo`, a **write-only** argument (Terraform 1.11+): Terraform sends it to Deed but never stores it in state or plan, and Deed never returns it. Change `secrets_wo_version` to send new values (rotation).

~> Destroying a source deletes every fact it contributed: entities only it declared are tombstoned and its tokens are revoked.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# GitHub connector: the token is write-only (never stored in state); bump secrets_wo_version to rotate it.
resource "deed_source" "github" {
  project       = deed_project.homelab.name
  name          = "github"
  provider_type = "github"
  config = jsonencode({
    owners        = ["example-org"]
    pull_requests = true
    issues        = true
  })
  secrets_wo         = { token = var.github_token }
  secrets_wo_version = 1
  schedule_seconds   = 900
}

# Terraform state read from an S3-compatible backend on the LAN.
resource "deed_source" "core_state" {
  project       = deed_project.homelab.name
  name          = "core-state"
  provider_type = "terraform_state"
  config = jsonencode({
    backend            = "s3"
    s3                 = { endpoint = "minio.example.com:9000", bucket = "tfstate", key = "core/terraform.tfstate" }
    workspace          = "core"
    infer_dependencies = true
    allow_cidrs        = ["192.168.10.0/24"]
  })
  secrets_wo = {
    s3_access_key_id     = var.state_reader_key_id
    s3_secret_access_key = var.state_reader_secret
  }
  secrets_wo_version = 1
  policy             = jsonencode({ on_absent = "tombstone", max_removal_percent = 25 })
}

# Pulse admin adapter (declared publish/subscribe grants and durable consumers).
resource "deed_source" "pulse" {
  project       = deed_project.homelab.name
  name          = "pulse"
  provider_type = "pulse_admin"
  config = jsonencode({
    admin_url     = "http://10.0.0.5:8080"
    insecure_http = true
    allow_cidrs   = ["10.0.0.0/24"]
  })
  secrets_wo         = { token = var.pulse_admin_token }
  secrets_wo_version = 1
}

# Push source fed by CI with source tokens (created in the UI or with the API).
resource "deed_source" "ci" {
  project                   = deed_project.homelab.name
  name                      = "ci-jobs"
  provider_type             = "push"
  expected_interval_seconds = 3600
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Source name, unique in the project. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `project` (String) Project name or ID. Changing it forces a new resource (the same project by name or ID does not).
- `provider_type` (String) Source provider: `github`, `hallpass`, `porch`, `terraform_state`, `pulse_admin`, `pulse_tail`, `push`, … (`GET /api/v1/providers`). Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `config` (String) Provider configuration as a JSON object string (use `jsonencode`), validated by Deed against the provider's schema. Secret fields do not belong here: put them in `secrets_wo`.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name. Defaults to `name`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the source runs and accepts data (default `true`).
- `expected_interval_seconds` (Number) How often data is expected (drives freshness for push sources). Defaults to Deed's choice.
- `layer` (String) Fact layer the source writes: `declared`, `imported`, `discovered` or `observation`. Defaults to the provider's layer. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `policy` (String) Reconciliation policy as a JSON object string: `priority`, `field_priority`, `on_absent` (`tombstone`, `orphan` or `keep`), `max_removal_percent`, `allowed_kinds`, `default_ttl_seconds`. Defaults to the provider's policy.
- `schedule_seconds` (Number) Pull interval in seconds (`0` = only on demand). Defaults to the provider's interval; always `0` for push-only providers.
- `secrets_wo` (Map of String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only credentials keyed by the provider's secret fields (for example `{ token = var.github_token }`). Sent on create and whenever `secrets_wo_version` changes; never stored in state. When the version changes and this is unset, the stored credentials are cleared.
- `secrets_wo_version` (Number) Change this (for example increment it, or use a 1Password item version) to send `secrets_wo` again.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Source ID (`src_…`).
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (`prj_…`).
- `pull` (Boolean) Whether Deed pulls from this source on a schedule.
- `push` (Boolean) Whether external programs push to this source with source tokens.
- `secret_fields_set` (Set of String) Secret fields that have a stored value in Deed (the values are never returned).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import deed_source.github homelab/github # <project>/<name>, or the source ID (src_…)
```
